Performers
Philadelphia Orchestra (orchestra), Leopold Stokowski (conductor) Documented[1] [3] [2]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition and any cuts or retouchings by the conductor are not identified in the sources consulted.

[1] [2]
Recorded
28 and 30 April 1927: part 1 on 28 April, parts 2 and 3 on 30 April Documented

Bolig dates CVE-29055 (part 1) to 28 April 1927 and CVE-29056 and CVE-29057 (parts 2 and 3) to 30 April 1927; the Internet Archive description and Pristine give the two session days for the symphony. Bolig calls the movement “Allegro con moto”; the usual marking is Andante con moto.

[3] [2] [1]
Place
Academy of Music, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States Documented[1] [3] [2]
Label
Victor Documented

Stokowski’s earlier acoustic recording of 1924 used the same matrix numbers without the CVE prefix and different issue numbers (Bolig lists 74894–⁠74897 and 6459–⁠6460); this transfer is the electrical recording of 1927 by its description, session dates and Victor numbers.

[1] [3] [2]
Catalogue
Victor 6663–⁠6665 (album M-16) Documented

The Internet Archive description says “Originally issued as Victor 6663, 6664 & 6665. (Later as a set as M-16.)”; Pristine gives the same numbers and album. Bolig also lists later Victor and HMV issues of the same sides. The disc and side on which the movement boundary falls are not identified; the allocation of matrices to movements follows Bolig’s part numbers.

[1] [2] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Parts 1–⁠3: CVE-29055, take 7 (Bolig) or take 6 (Pristine); CVE-29056, take 7; CVE-29057, take 7 Disputed: sources disagree

The two discographic sources agree on the matrices and on takes 7 for CVE-29056 and CVE-29057 but differ on the take of CVE-29055. Neither can be checked against a label image here, and the DAHR matrix pages could not be opened on 17 October 2026 (503 error).

  • CVE-29055, take 7 — Bolig.
  • CVE-29055, take 6 — Pristine producer’s note.
[3] [2]
Transfer
Bob Varney Documented

The Internet Archive description reads “Transfer by Bob Varney”.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is identified. The Internet Archive item was added on 24 January 2011, which is an upload date.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

The stylus, equalisation, speed and noise treatment are not documented. The file runs 11:55; Pristine’s own restoration runs 12:00, so the two transfers differ by a few seconds, and where the side joins fall in this file is not known.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Schubert died in 1828. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

[5] [6]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

The Internet Archive item carries a CC0 licence URL declared by the uploader, which is not treated as authority to waive Victor’s rights. The pre-1963 European rule applies because the recording was made in 1927 and was on sale by January 1928 (a Victor advertisement in The Golden Book Magazine offers Records Nos. 6663-4-5), so the 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension; the exact first issue date is not established. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence. The recording was published after 1925, so a US public-domain basis is not established.

  • Pre-1963 European public domain — territorial basis.
  • CC0 — licence URL on the Internet Archive item, uploader’s declaration.

Franz Schubert, Symphony No. 8 in B minor “Unfinished”, II. Andante con moto; Philadelphia Orchestra, Leopold Stokowski, April 1927. Victor 6663–⁠6665 (album M-16); transfer by Bob Varney, Internet Archive. Rights metadata conflicts; public domain in the EU only; no worldwide recording clearance is asserted. Rights statement
